issues.detail: Missing error handling for RBAC permission failures, kubectl access issues, timeout scenarios, and malformed metric responses.

scenarios.name: production-waste-analysis
scenarios.rationale: Both lack actual data to compute efficiency ratios or waste estimates, but B demonstrates deep understanding of K8s optimization (p99 baseline vs point-in-time, VPA, Prometheus queries) and explicitly flags data limitations per the rubric; A questions whether K8s exists in the repo despite the user's clear statement of $50k/month K8s costs, missing the assumption and offering less actionable guidance toward satisfying the rubric.

scenarios.name: staging-zombie-cleanup
scenarios.rationale: Response A declines to help and asks for clarification instead of providing methodology; Response B delivers actionable kubectl commands to find zero-CPU deployments, check metadata, and delete—covering CPU detection, deletion commands, and team coordination warning—but omits estimated monthly waste calculation and explicit 7-day data-span verification in its workflow.

scenarios.name: oomkill-prevention-sizing
scenarios.rationale: Response A asks diagnostic questions appropriately but provides an interim YAML example that violates the rubric (limit ≠ request: 2Gi vs 1Gi), omits risk level, lacks CPU, and skips kustomize patch format. Response B delivers a formula-driven right-sizing method with correct limit=request, explicit 30% buffer rationale, proper RFC 6902 JSON patches, and a concrete example—but both miss CPU recommendations and Response B lacks explicit risk assignment.
